reason: The support is still a single-author study with a small sample (arXiv:2609.00072: 21 induced failures across 10 MCP servers), and confidence is low. No replication has been recorded since 2026-09-28. MCP spec 2025-06-18 offers isError, structuredContent/outputSchema and the idempotentHint/destructiveHint annotations, but these are per-tool hints with no fidelity guarantee and no per-error replay-safety field. The protocol gap is therefore plausible but not confirmed beyond one study. Keep unverified.

evidence.summary: Typed fields expose that a failure occurred (18/21) but rarely its cause, repair or replay safety; single author, small sample.
isError plus structuredContent/outputSchema available; annotations are untrusted hints (recorded in RMD-MCPERRACT-001).
candidate; typed error payload with cause, retriable and retry_after on the server side, plus a client-side replay policy.

model_assessment.assessment: Protocol and server-design gap. Model improvement can only partly compensate through heuristics.

remedy_assessment.assessment: Current candidate. Complements RMD-TOOLEFFECT-001 for P-20260831-3039ED15.

reopen_triggers: another study reproduces insufficient MCP error actionability
MCP spec adds error actionability or replay-safety fields
